task_instruction: Review the attached file (tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/review_target.py) for Clean Architecture and SOLID violations, per this repo's rules/coding-standards.md. For each violation: cite the file:line, name the specific principle violated, state its severity, and suggest a fix. Do not fix the code yourself -- produce a review report only.
completion_threshold_rationale: Pre-registered alongside the rubric, before any run: a review counts as a completed task only if it correctly identifies both structural violations that make this fixture worth reviewing at all -- magic_number (2pts) + srp_mixed_io_logic (3pts) = 5/10. The other four criteria (swallowed_error, file_line_citations, severity_proportional, no_fabrication) are quality-of-execution refinements on top of a review that already found the two load-bearing issues; a review that misses both structural violations but nails citation formatting has not completed the reviewing task this benchmark is measuring, regardless of its point total. This is a defensible, stated rule chosen by the task author before results existed, not a round-number global cutoff (coding-standards.md §8: no invented constants).

rubric.criterion: Identifies the unnamed/unsourced discount threshold (500) and multiplier (0.9) as a magic-number violation (coding-standards.md §3.1).
Identifies that process_order mixes I/O (DB read, HTTP call) with business logic (discount calculation) in one function -- an SRP/layering violation (§1.1, §3.1).
Identifies the silent `return None` on a non-200 payment response as an unnamed failure mode / swallowed error (§9 anti-pattern list).
Every reported finding cites a specific file:line, not just a general description.
Severity assigned is proportional to consequence (the SRP/payment-flow issues are ranked at or above the magic number, not flooded with equal-weight style nits).
Reports no violation that is not actually present in the fixture (no false positives).
